title: ci(release): use i686 musl toolchain for i686 binary
body:
The i686 release job failed to build. It used the apt glibc cross gcc (`i686-linux-gnu-gcc`) for the `i686-unknown-linux-musl` target, which has no 32-bit headers on a clean runner and is the wrong libc for a musl target, so `zstd-sys` failed at `bits/libc-header-start.h`.

Fetch a prebuilt i686 musl cross toolchain (Bootlin `x86-i686--musl--stable-2024.05-1`) instead and point the CC, linker, and payload CC at its `i686-linux-gcc`. It compiles the C dependencies, links the static musl binary, and builds the freestanding payloads.

Validated locally with a clean environment: `cargo build --locked --target i686-unknown-linux-musl` produces a statically linked i386 binary that runs and reports the correct version.

title: feat(i686): add 32-bit x86 target and native runtime support
body:
## Summary

Adds full 32-bit x86 (i686) support to onelf: the injected payloads, the ELF32 rewriter, a native i686 runtime, a real-32-bit-distro smoke test, and (as cleanup) an in-tree userland-exec that removes the last external blocker to i686 shipping on crates.io.

## What's included

- **i686 target support** — `EM_386` dispatch, an i686 bootstrap trampoline (`call`/`pop` PC-relative, `int 0x80`) plus a 32-bit `_onelf_bootstrap` twin, an i686 `onelf-env` constructor, an ELF32 branch in `inject_relative_interp`, `i386` multiarch lib dirs, and the `build.rs` plumbing (payload entry, `payload_cc`, `x86`→`i686` arch normalization).
- **All-arch bss fix** — `map_interp` only zeroed a bss segment up to `memsz`, but a file mapping exposes the file's own bytes between `filesz` and the page boundary; the loader's malloc arena lives in `[memsz, page_end)`, so the main link_map started on garbage and `dl_main` crashed dereferencing an un-zeroed `l_info` slot. Now zeroes the full partial page. This was latent on x86_64/aarch64 too and is fixed for all arches.
- **Native i686 runtime** — building onelf for `i686-unknown-linux-musl` now produces packages whose outer executable is a 32-bit i386 static runtime (versus cross-packing on x86_64, which embeds the x86_64 runtime). Needed an i686 signal restorer in the FUSE path (the legacy non-rt sigframe: `pop`/`sigreturn`, not `rt_sigreturn`, since the handler sets `SA_RESTORER` without `SA_SIGINFO`) and taught `find_musl_gcc` the bootlin `x86-i686-musl` path.
- **In-tree userland-exec** — replaces the external `userland-execve` crate (x86_64/aarch64-only) with a small implementation on `rustix` + `goblin`. This drops the `nix` dependency and a duplicate `goblin 0.8`, adds i686, and removes the need for any vendored fork or `[patch.crates-io]`, so the published `onelf-rt` supports all three arches. Also fixes `read_elf_interp`, which only read the first 8 KB and so missed `.interp` after `patchelf` relocates it, leaving the ulexec path unreachable.
- **i386-container smoke test** — `scripts/smoke-i386.sh` builds a native i686 package and runs it inside an i386 container via podman (native through the kernel's IA32 support, no qemu). It self-skips when the toolchains or podman are absent, and is wired into `cargo test` behind `ONELF_SMOKE_I386=1`.

## Test plan

Verified end-to-end on an x86_64 host with the bootlin i686 toolchains and podman:

- i686 packages (PIE and non-PIE, glibc and musl) bundle, pack, and run — on the host via the kernel's IA32 support, and inside real 32-bit distros: `i386/debian` (glibc, all exec modes) and `i386/alpine` (musl-only, no glibc — proving self-containment).
- The native i686 package runs its default/fuse/cache modes; `memfd` is incompatible with relative-interp bootstrap binaries on every arch (a pre-existing limitation, so such binaries aren't memfd-eligible by default).
- The in-tree ulexec verified for x86_64 glibc, i686 glibc (bundled glibc 2.41 loading correctly against a system 2.36 — the cross-version case that proves it uses the bundled loader), and i686 musl.
- Full suite green (unit + pipeline), `cargo fmt`/`clippy` clean, and `cargo package -p onelf` / `-p onelf-rt` package cleanly with no patch.

## Dependency note

Building the native i686 runtime and running the smoke test require the bootlin i686 cross toolchains under `/opt/bootlin/x86-i686-{glibc,musl}`, provided by the `bootlin-toolchain-i686-*` ebuilds in the sibling gentoo-x overlay. CI or reviewers without them will build the default (host-arch) runtime fine and simply skip the smoke test, which self-skips when its prerequisites are missing.

title: onelf-env exec interposer + AppRun launcher; bake rpath on bundled libraries
body:
## Summary

Strengthens bundled-library resolution for the execution paths onelf's launcher does **not** front, and keeps the baked `$ORIGIN` rpath that `main` already relied on.

The branch initially explored an rpath-free model (an env-independent exec interposer plus `--library-path`), but a real failure showed why rpath is still required: a bundled binary invoked **outside** the launcher (a wrapper shell script execing it through the host `/bin/sh`, as in the miniflux example) has no launcher in the loop. So the baked `$ORIGIN` rpath stays; the new interposer and AppRun cover the cases rpath alone can't.

## What's genuinely new vs `main`

- **`onelf-env` exec-family interposer** (`execve`/`execv`/`execvp`/`execvpe`/`posix_spawn`/`posix_spawnp`): a freestanding, self-locating constructor that survives `clearenv()` + re-exec (Chromium/Electron/Steam zygotes). It re-applies `.onelf/env` and, for host children, strips `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`/`LD_PRELOAD`/`ONELF_*` so the bundled libc never leaks.
- **`.onelf/libpath`** written at pack time so the interposer rebuilds the bundle lib path without depending on the environment.
- **`AppRun` launcher** (`bundle-libs --apprun`) for running an unpacked AppDir through the bundled dynamic linker (the cross-libc case, e.g. a glibc bundle on a musl host).
- **One rpath change** (see below).

## The rpath part is mostly what `main` already had

`main` (v0.2.8) already baked `$ORIGIN/../lib` via `patchelf --force-rpath --set-rpath` in `set_origin_runpath`. An earlier commit on this branch removed it (the rpath-free experiment); a later commit restored it. Those two were squashed, so there is no net drop-then-re-add churn — the rpath core ends up identical to `main`.

**The one real rpath change:** drop `main`'s `if !is_executable { return NotNeeded }` gate so the `$ORIGIN` rpath is baked on **shared libraries too**, not just executables. `main`'s own comment assumed a library resolves its deps "via the executable's DT_RUNPATH (transitive search)" — which is false. glibc does **not** apply an executable's rpath to a *library's own* children, so `libpq` (which ships no rpath slot) could not find `libssl`. Giving each bundled library its own `$ORIGIN` rpath fixes transitive resolution. (`--force-rpath` on the `onelf-env --add-needed` keeps patchelf from downgrading the baked `DT_RPATH` to `DT_RUNPATH`; that's coupled to the new injection.)

## Docs

- `bundling.md`, `environment.md`, `env-vars.md`, `cli.md` describe the model (launcher `--library-path` + baked `$ORIGIN` rpath + interposer).
- miniflux example: place postgres extensions at the host's `pkglibdir` leaf (`lib/postgresql/`), derived with `realpath --relative-to` so it's correct on any distro. Flat `lib/` failed on Arch/Alpine with `could not access file "dict_snowball"`.

## Verification

- Full miniflux + embedded PostgreSQL stack end to end on a glibc host: cluster init (incl. the `dict_snowball` tsearch step), 125 migrations, admin user, HTTP server, `GET /healthcheck → 200`.
- Standalone repro (shell script execing a bundled `curl` with a transitive lib chain via host `/bin/sh`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=''`): every bundled lib resolves through the baked rpath alone.
- `cargo test` green (19 tests), including the `clearenv` re-exec and bin-on-PATH cases.

## Known follow-up (not in this PR)

`onelf pack` does not exclude its own output file, so an in-place `onelf build` packs the previous output into the new one and sizes snowball. Worth a small fix (skip the resolved output path when it lives inside the packed dir); deferred.
